channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral nas ruas e propaganda virtual começam neste domingo
item.description: The electoral campaign for Brazil's 2026 elections officially began this Sunday (16), allowing candidates to conduct in-person activities such as caravans, marches, and leafleting between 8 a.m. and 10 p.m. Virtual propaganda is also permitted, marking the official start of campaigning both on the streets and online.

item.title: Zema inicia disputa eleitoral com provocação a Lula nas redes
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for the Novo party, launched his campaign with a provocative social media video featuring a paper airplane bearing the message 'Untouchables belong in jail! I’m coming… Zema' directed at President Lula. The post, made on Sunday (August 16), coincided with the TSE’s authorization for electoral propaganda in public spaces and online, signaling the official start of the presidential race.

item.title: Romero Jucá registra candidatura após Dino suspender condenação
item.description: Romero Jucá (MDB-RR) registered his candidacy for federal deputy from Roraima on Saturday, the 15th, after Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the effects of a conviction that could have made him ineligible. A provisional injunction from the STF and STJ nullified the conviction's effects, allowing Jucá to run in the 2026 election. The candidacy was first reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Em 1ª live de campanha, Renan fala em vingança e critica Lula e Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) officially launched his presidential campaign in a YouTube live stream that peaked at 27,000 viewers, advocating for harsher police operations against organized crime and proposing a 'Nuremberg of the Favelas' to posthumously prosecute deceased criminals. He accused Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro of corruption, linking Lula to alleged INSS fund diversions and Flávio to investigations involving Daniel Vorcaro, and suggested a potential runoff between them could be 'settled at Vorcaro’s house in Trancoso'.

item.title: Programa de Flávio dá continuidade à transição energética de Lula 3
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) proposes continuity in Lula's energy transition, focusing on biofuels, decarbonization, and modernization of the electricity sector. His government plan aligns with the current petista administration's guidelines, including ethanol and biodiesel expansion, strengthening RenovaBio, and investing in energy storage.

item.title: Plano de Flávio não menciona Petrobras, e Lula cita estatal 11 vezes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s 75-page government plan for the 2026 presidential race makes no mention of Petrobras, despite advocating for expanded gas exploration in the pre-salt, fracking, and reviving the National Privatization Program. In contrast, Lula’s plan references the state oil company 11 times, positioning it at the core of Brazil’s energy policy. Flávio argues the state’s role is to ensure the country functions, not to act as a businessman, and proposes case-by-case evaluation of privatization.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro deve muito à Michelle, sua madrasta
item.description: The rapprochement between Flávio Bolsonaro and his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro was described by Noblat's panel as a staged, short-lived arrangement, taking place during a barbecue at the party headquarters in Brasília. While it boosted Flávio’s standing among evangelicals and women in the Quaest poll, the alliance is seen as a survival tactic for him and a long-term investment for Michelle, who aims to serve eight years in the Senate from the DF to position herself for a 2030 presidential run. Flávio risks losing his seat and special STF immunity if defeated in 2026.

item.title: Tensões diplomáticas tendem a agravar distanciamento comercial entre Brasil e Argentina
item.description: The strategic partnership between Brazil and Argentina, Latin America's most important, is at its worst point in decades due to diplomatic tensions between Argentine President Javier Milei and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, marked by mutual insults, ambassador withdrawals, and a cooling of trade flows. Although Argentina's economic crisis is reducing its import demand, Brazil has been disproportionately affected by the decline in Argentine imports compared to other partners like China and the U.S. While Brazil-Argentina trade fell 18% in the first half of 2026, Argentine exports to China and the U.S. surged by 42% and 63%, respectively, signaling a strategic shift away from Brazil, particularly in the automotive sector where cross-border production chains are being disrupted.

item.title: A inesperada vaia a Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faced unexpected jeers in Rio de Janeiro following the revelation of his proximity to Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the sponsorship of the film 'Dark Horse'. The incident, described as a 'displeasure' for the senator, occurred in May and provoked negative reactions even outside direct electoral contexts. The subscriber-only article suggests the episode reflects image wear tied to controversial associations.

item.title: Cleitinho declara patrimônio de R$ 956 mil ao TSE
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG) registered his candidacy for governor of Minas Gerais with the TSE on August 14, 2026, declaring assets worth R$ 956,564.03. After uncertainty due to personal reasons, including his brother's death, he was confirmed as the party's candidate on August 7, running in a pure ticket with Luís Eduardo Falcão as his running mate.

item.title: “Evidente que vamos mudar a regra”, diz Marinho sobre arcabouço fiscal
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, states he intends to replace the current fiscal framework with a new rule aimed at reducing public debt and achieving primary surpluses, though he has not disclosed the formula. Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), campaign political coordinator, confirmed the change is evident and necessary.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro registra candidatura ao Senado pelo DF
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro registered her candidacy for the Senate in the Federal District on Saturday, the 15th, shortly before the TSE deadline. This will be her first run for public office, running under number 222. In the DF, voters will elect two senators in this election.

item.title: Renan Santos critica mais Flávio Bolsonaro do que Lula nas redes
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) more than Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) on social media between June 1 and August 11, 2024, with 45 posts targeting the senator and 42 targeting the president, including 14 posts that criticized both simultaneously. His criticisms of Flávio centered on corruption suspicions (rachadinha, Dark Horse film funding) and the claim that he 'is not right-wing', while critiques of Lula focused on economic issues such as public debt and social programs. Renan favored Instagram for his statements, where he criticized Lula more, while on X he posted more against Flávio.

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha comprou joias para Marcola de Lula
item.description: Federal Police investigators discovered that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger paid for two jewelry items selected by Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, to gift relatives of Lula’s former chief of staff for Mother’s Day 2024. The transactions were revealed via WhatsApp messages and PF investigations, reported by Globo.

item.title: Flávio é orientado a focar nas cidades mais bolsonaristas do Nordeste
item.description: Bolsonarist leaders advised Flávio Bolsonaro to focus his 2026 campaign on Northeastern cities where the gap between Lula and Jair Bolsonaro was smallest in 2022, such as São Bento (PB), aiming to 'lose by less' in the region to improve the national outcome. The Northeast was Lula’s main electoral stronghold in 2022, with 22.5 million votes versus Bolsonaro’s 10 million, a 12.6 million advantage. The strategy seeks to mirror the impact of a strong performance in states like São Paulo, potentially bolstered by Michelle Bolsonaro’s presence.

item.title: “Honestino é agente do seu tempo”, diz diretor de filme sobre o ativista
item.description: Director Aurélio Michiles released the documentary 'Honestino', portraying the life and disappearance of student activist Honestino Guimarães during Brazil's military dictatorship. The film blends archival footage, dramatic reenactments, and testimonies, inspired by a video of the activist’s grandson and a personal archive from his former partner, Isaura Botelho. Michiles emphasized Honestino’s humanity, recalling moments of lightness like going to see Fellini’s 'Satyricon', and his dream of a world where social justice prevailed.

item.title: TSE firma acordo contra clonagem de voz nas eleições
item.description: The TSE has signed a technical cooperation agreement with ElevenLabs to prevent fraudulent voice cloning in the 2026 elections, establishing a protective mechanism to block unauthorized synthetic voices, track manipulated audio, and enhance accessibility via voice tools. The partnership, with no financial transfers, supports the Electoral Justice’s Permanent Program to Combat Disinformation and aims to safeguard public figures from AI-generated audio deepfakes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro está 'cansado'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, was described by close allies as 'tired' and 'a bit scattered' last week, despite the official campaign start still being 49 days away for the first round and 70 for the second. The subscriber-exclusive article highlights internal concerns about his energy and focus in the 2026 electoral race.

item.title: Jair Bolsonaro ainda é o político com mais seguidores nas redes; veja ranking
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro remains the Brazilian politician with the highest number of social media followers, totaling 67.2 million across Instagram, X, YouTube, TikTok, and Facebook. The subscriber-exclusive article emphasizes his enduring digital influence despite ongoing judicial and political restrictions.

item.title: Planos de governo de presidenciáveis têm de 2 a 200 páginas
item.description: The article notes that government plans from presidential candidates for the 2026 elections range from 2 to 200 pages, reflecting varying levels of detail and complexity in their proposals. It mentions that the little-known party Unidade Popular, which registered a candidacy with the TSE in 2019, is running again for the Presidency in 2026. The content is presented as a subscriber-exclusive article, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Entorno de Lula não crê em conversa com Trump antes da eleição; saiba o motivo
item.description: Lula said he intends to speak with Donald Trump to address pending issues between Brazil and the U.S., but his inner circle doubts he will do so before the 2026 election. They believe such a meeting would depend on a post-election context, given the electoral calendar and domestic priorities.

item.title: Lula e Flávio usam redutos históricos para dar a largada em corrida acirrada ao Planalto
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro officially launch their 2026 presidential campaigns in symbolic events: Lula at Estádio 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo, the birthplace of his union activism; Flávio at Copacabana Beach, aiming to tie himself to his father Jair Bolsonaro’s legacy. A Quaest poll shows a technical tie in a potential runoff (43% to 40%) and Lula leading in the first round (38% to 31%).

item.title: Campanha de Lula resgata passado sindical e levará metalúrgicos ao palco em 1º ato
item.description: Lula's 2026 re-election campaign will launch its opening act in São Bernardo do Campo, ABC Paulista, under the theme 'Where it all began'. The event will feature metalworkers on stage, highlighting Lula's unionist roots, and include testimonies from social program beneficiaries, alongside the unveiling of a new slogan ('Brazil ready for more') and an updated campaign jingle.

item.title: Pix e Panda Bonds: Brasil aprofunda relação financeira com a China
item.description: Brazil is deepening its financial cooperation with China, planning to issue its first yuan-denominated sovereign bond (panda bond) this year, worth 5 billion yuan, as part of a strategy to reduce dependence on the U.S. dollar. At the same time, China seeks to integrate its payment systems, including Union Pay, with Brazil’s Pix, enabling smoother transactions for Chinese tourists and strengthening bilateral ties amid rising tensions with the United States.

item.title: VÍDEO: para que servem as pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: Electoral polls function as a thermometer of the election, helping to understand the scenario of the dispute. They can be spontaneous or stimulated, are conducted by specialized institutes and can be commissioned by media outlets, companies and other interested parties. During the electoral period, polling companies must follow the rules of the Electoral Justice, with methodology, contractor and payer available in the TSE system.

item.title: Kotscho: Lula volta ao estádio de Vila Euclides, onde tudo começou
item.description: Lula returns to Vila Euclides Stadium, the birthplace of his political journey, evoking memories of the ABC strikes, the imprisonment of metalworkers’ leaders, amnesty, the return of exiles, the founding of the PT and CUT, and the struggle for the Constituent Assembly in the late 1970s and early 1980s. The return symbolizes the continuity of his fight for workers and democracy.

item.title: Pai, filho, sobrinho e irmã: o palanque familiar de Motta na Paraíba
item.description: The electoral dispute in Paraíba is turning into a battlefield of family alliances around the group of Congressman Hugo Motta (Republicans), with efforts to secure President Lula’s support. The movement involves close relatives such as father, son, nephew, and sister, forming a 'family platform' in local political maneuvering.

item.title: Tarcísio faz mega-aliança por reeleição em SP, e Haddad gruda em Lula
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) launches his re-election campaign for governor of São Paulo, aiming to consolidate his mandate after defeating Fernando Haddad in 2022. Haddad, meanwhile, seeks to return the Palácio dos Bandeirantes to the PT, which has never governed the state. The race repeats the 2022 matchup, but under a changed political landscape.

item.title: PF descobre que lobista do Careca do INSS comprou duas joias para ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula
item.description: The Federal Police discovered that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Fábio Luiz Lula da Silva and linked to the 'Careca do INSS' scheme, bought two jewelry pieces to gift relatives of Marco Aurélio Ribeiro, known as Marcola, former chief of staff to Lula, for Mother's Day 2024. The jewelry was purchased at Marcola's request as part of an alleged network of illicit favors and benefits. The exclusive subscriber-only article details ongoing investigations into corruption and influence peddling involving figures close to the government.

item.title: Eleições 2026: entenda o ‘politiquês’ em um glossário para acompanhar o noticiário eleitoral
item.description: Estadão has released a glossary to help the public understand the political jargon of the 2026 electoral campaign, which officially begins on August 16. The glossary explains terms such as abstention, economic power abuse, AIJE, AIME, and anti-establishment, with examples like Jair Bolsonaro's case. It also covers the renewal of two-thirds of the Senate and the possibility of a fourth presidential term, an unprecedented event in Brazil's history.

item.title: Governo impõe sigilo em pedido de retorno de delegados da PF cedidos em meio a casos Master e INSS
item.description: The Ministry of Justice imposed secrecy on a list of federal police officers seconded to courts that the government requested to return to the PF, claiming the measure is still in a preparatory phase and aims to strengthen public security. The move is seen by PF and judiciary officials as a possible retaliation against delegate Thiago Marcantonio, who works in the office of Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça. Justice Minister Wellington César Lima e Silva repeatedly refused to disclose information about the memo, even under Freedom of Information Act requests.

item.title: Campanha tem início com Lula em São Bernardo e Flávio no Rio; veja agenda dos outros candidatos
item.description: The presidential campaign began on Sunday, the 16th, with Lula (PT) launching his candidacy in São Bernardo do Campo, the birthplace of his union leadership, and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) starting his in Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro, both focusing on the Southeast region. Lula leads with 38% voting intention, followed by Flávio at 31%, while other candidates trail significantly. The events emphasize historical symbolism and regional strategy, with Lula revisiting his working-class roots and Flávio mobilizing the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Bolsonaristas querem que Michelle faça ao menos 2 viagens na eleição
item.description: Bolsonarist leaders are urging former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro to make at least two trips during the 2026 campaign — one in São Paulo and another in the Northeast — to support PL candidates for governor, deputy, and senator. However, Michelle has indicated she intends to focus on Brasília due to her caregiving responsibilities for imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro and her own Senate campaign in the Federal District, where she plans to rely on social media and female mobilization.

item.title: PL dos Minerais Críticos deve ser apensado para acelerar o trâmite
item.description: The Critical Minerals Bill, approved in the Chamber of Deputies and stalled in the Senate by Davi Alcolumbre, is set to be attached to an older bill in the Infrastructure Committee to speed up its processing, following realignment between Senate leadership and the Lula government. The bill distinguishes critical from strategic minerals, creates the CMCE to review international agreements posing national security risks, and is part of the federal government’s sovereignty strategy amid tensions with the United States.

item.title: Campanha começa neste domingo. Veja o que é permitido até 4 de outubro
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian electoral campaign officially begins on Sunday, August 16, allowing explicit vote requests, live streams, rallies, and paid press and internet advertising until October 2. Rules set by the TSE aim to ensure fairness, following the close of candidate registration at 7 p.m. on Saturday, August 15. Paid online content boosting is permitted until October 1, but officials including the president and heads of Congress and the Supreme Court are barred from using broadcast networks for political propaganda or attacks on parties.

item.title: Lula e Flávio iniciam campanha com corrida eleitoral acirrada
item.description: The 2026 presidential race between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is extremely tight, with recent polls showing a technical tie or minimal lead for Lula, contrasting sharply with his large advantage over Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. Latest surveys from Quaest, Datafolha, and CNT/MDA reveal fluctuating leads, with differences of 3 to 9 percentage points in a potential runoff — all within or near the margin of error. This closeness reflects a more polarized and unpredictable political landscape than in previous elections.

item.title: Candidatos dão a largada na corrida presidencial neste domingo (16/8)
item.description: Presidential candidates launched their campaigns on Sunday (August 16), with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) starting in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) on Copacabana Beach (RJ), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Renan Santos (Missão) also choosing their political strongholds to begin the race, following TSE authorization for street and online electoral propaganda.

item.title: Os ventos da política
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) remains central in electoral debates, signaling its growing influence in national politics. The right supports Flavio Bolsonaro due to lack of a better alternative, warning of the risk of a fourth Lula government, which could appoint four new STF justices and dominate the plenary, deciding fundamental national issues.

item.title: Campanha de Renan diz ter R$ 2 milhões de vaquinha e venda de livro
item.description: Renan Santos' (Missão) campaign claims to have raised R$ 2 million for his 2026 presidential bid, sourced from an online fundraiser (R$ 1.3 million) and sales of the 'Yellow Book' (R$ 1 million). Inspired by Javier Milei's ultraliberalism, the campaign relies on MBL volunteers, avoids professional consultants, uses commercial flights, and expects up to R$ 3 million more from the Electoral Fund — to be shared among gubernatorial, congressional, and senatorial candidates.

item.title: Flávio fecha acordo com autor de deepfakes que o associavam a Hitler
item.description: Influencer Roger Prado da Fonseca reached an agreement with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential pre-candidate, after publishing three false deepfakes linking him to Hitler, stealing from retirees, and corruption. The deal requires a public apology on Instagram for at least ten days and payment of five minimum wages in 12 installments to a social entity designated by the court, plus a ban on further offensive posts.

item.title: Admar Gonzaga, advogado de Garotinho, votou pela inelegibilidade dele no TSE
item.description: Admar Gonzaga, current lawyer for Anthony Garotinho, voted for his ineligibility at the TSE in 2018 while serving as a minister. Garotinho was convicted of administrative improbity in the diversion of R$234.3 million in the 'Saúde em Movimento' project, with the conviction becoming final in August 2018 and political rights suspended until August 2026. Gonzaga's defense claims the penalty has already been served, despite a recent TJ-RJ ruling ordering full compliance with the sentence.

item.title: Flávio abre campanha com foco em segurança e pede votos para o Senado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launched his presidential campaign with a live broadcast, criticizing the PT and Lula’s government, and presented proposals on security, economy, and education. He urged votes for PL-backed candidates in the states, aiming to secure a Senate majority, as 54 of 81 seats are up for election. The campaign officially began Sunday with an event in Copacabana, electoral propaganda is now authorized, and the first round is set for October 4, 2026.

item.title: Entrevista: 'Classe C não enxerga Lula ou Flávio como passaporte para futuro melhor', diz presidente do Locomotiva
item.description: Renato Meirelles states that Brazil's C class — representing 53% of the population with an average income of R$3,500 — lost political connection after 2013, when the 'decade of optimism' ended. Despite benefiting from policies like minimum wage increases and formal employment, this group believes its progress came from individual effort, not government action, and no longer sees Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro as symbols of a better future. The sense of stagnation has fueled an anti-system sentiment, as the C class blames the government for failing to meet expectations it helped create.

item.title: Tema central na campanha que começa hoje, medo de ser assaltado alcança dois a cada três eleitores, aponta pesquisa
item.description: The Ideia poll reveals that 66% of Brazilians fear or greatly fear being victim of an armed robbery, and 63.9% fear having their cellphone stolen, making insecurity a central theme in the 2026 electoral campaign, cited by candidates across the political spectrum. The data, obtained exclusively by GLOBO, shows that the sense of insecurity affects the majority of the population.

item.title: Violência pauta voto para presidente de 63% dos eleitores de direita, contra 45% à esquerda, revela pesquisa Ideia
item.description: The Ideia poll shows public safety is a priority for 45.7% of voters in the presidential race, but with strong polarization: 63.7% of Bolsonarist right-wing voters consider it crucial for their presidential vote, compared to only 45.6% of non-Lulist left-wing voters. Conversely, for state governments, non-Lulist left-wing voters prioritize security in 62.2% of cases, while Bolsonarist right-wing voters do so in 44.6%, indicating a perceived inversion of responsibility across government levels.

item.title: Lula 'farmando aura': aos 80 anos, petista tenta rejuvenescer imagem para atrair eleitorado mais jovem
item.description: Lula's re-election campaign, at age 80, is attempting to rejuvenate his image by adopting youth-associated language, gestures, and social media trends—such as gaming slang, K-pop hand signs, and TikTok content—to appeal to younger voters and counter perceptions of political fatigue. The strategy includes portraying him as a 'friend of millennials,' emphasizing his 1970s union activism as anti-establishment symbolism, and highlighting his gym routine and whey protein use to convey vitality. The campaign launch at Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo features archival footage of Lula leading strikes in the ABC region to reinforce this narrative.

item.title: Em meio a incômodo com desempenho nas redes, Flávio Bolsonaro escala aliados para alavancar presença digital
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is seeking to boost its digital presence by mobilizing allies to counter attacks and amplify messages, reducing his personal reliance on social media. This strategy arises from his low engagement compared to Michelle Bolsonaro, whose video received nearly eight times more views. Despite the strong online presence of the far right, Flávio's campaign struggles to convert the accumulated digital capital of Bolsonarism into effective support for his candidacy.

item.title: Renan Santos escolhe SP, palco que projetou MBL, para lançar campanha
item.description: Renan Santos, former founder of the MBL, officially launches his presidential campaign for the Partido Missão in an event at Largo São Francisco, São Paulo, featuring speeches by Amanda Vettorazzo, Kim Kataguiri, and Aroldo Medina. The event, scheduled for Sunday (August 16), is expected to gather around 2,000 people, highlighting his opposition to the PT and advocacy for liberal economic policies. His campaign includes criticism of the Lula government and a proposal to involve the Federal Police in investigating alleged electoral irregularities.

item.title: Vox: Marina, Tebet e André do Prado lideram corrida ao Senado em SP
item.description: Marina Silva (Rede) leads the Senate race in São Paulo with 26.1% of voting intentions, followed by Simone Tebet (MDB) at 25.5% and André do Prado (PL) at 21.5%, according to a Vox Brasil Institute poll. With a 2.55-point margin of error and 53.9% of voters undecided, the race remains highly open and competitive.

item.title: Vox: Tarcísio tem 53,7% e Haddad, 34% no 1º turno em São Paulo
item.description: The Vox Brasil poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading with 53.7% of voting intentions and Fernando Haddad (PT) at 34% in the first round for São Paulo governor, suggesting a likely first-round victory even accounting for the 2.55-point margin of error. In the second round, Tarcísio holds 54.3% against Haddad's 35.2%, and in valid votes reaches 60.7% versus Haddad's 39.3%. Tarcísio has 66.5% approval and 22.3% rejection, while Haddad has 46.1% rejection.
